record.context_brief: minimizing spectral radius for paired odd cycles
record.original_question: For a signed graph consisting of 2k odd cycles of pairwise equal length and opposite signs, is the signature described in Proposition 3.27 the signature that minimizes spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Proposition 3.27. Let Γ be a signed graph consisting of 2k odd cycles of pairwise equal length and opposite signs. Then ρ(Γ) < 2 √ 4k − 1.
Is the signature in Proposition 3.27 the one minimizing the spectral radius? We leave this as an open problem (see also [85]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A signed graph is a pair $\Gamma=(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a signature. The (signed) adjacency matrix $A_\sigma$ of $\Gamma$ has $(A_\sigma)_{uv}=\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. The spectral radius of $\Gamma$ is $\rho(\Gamma)=\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\text{ is an eigenvalue of }A_\sigma\}$. The sign of a cycle $C$ in $\Gamma$ is $\sigma(C)=\prod_{e\in E(C)}\sigma(e)\in\{+1,-1\}$; the cycle is called positive (resp. negative) accordingly. Two signatures $\sigma,\sigma'$ on $G$ are switching-equivalent if there exists $\theta:V\to\{+1,-1\}$ such that $\sigma'(uv)=\theta(u)\sigma(uv)\theta(v)$ for every edge $uv$; switching-equivalent signatures yield similar adjacency matrices and hence the same spectrum.

Setup. Fix an integer $k\ge 1$ and an odd integer $\ell\ge 3$. Let $G$ be the graph obtained from $2k$ vertex-disjoint cycles of common length $\ell$ by identifying one vertex of each cycle to a single common vertex (so $G$ is a bouquet of $2k$ odd cycles of equal length sharing a single vertex). On $G$ consider the signature $\sigma^\star$ in which exactly $k$ of the $2k$ cycles are positive and the remaining $k$ are negative (this signature, up to switching equivalence, depends only on which cycles are positive and which are negative, and any two such signatures with the same partition of cycles into $k$ positive and $k$ negative are switching-equivalent). It is known that the resulting signed graph $\Gamma^\star=(G,\sigma^\star)$ satisfies $\rho(\Gamma^\star)<2\sqrt{4k-1}$.

Question. Among all signatures $\sigma$ on the underlying graph $G$, does $\sigma^\star$ achieve the minimum value of the spectral radius $\rho((G,\sigma))$? Equivalently, prove or disprove that $\rho((G,\sigma))\ge\rho(\Gamma^\star)$ for every signature $\sigma$ of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2019 survey on open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs (Belardo–Cioabă–Koolen–Wang). Subsequent literature on extremal spectral radii of signed graphs (e.g., works on unbalanced signed graphs with extremal index, signed bipartite graphs, etc.) does not appear to address or resolve this specific minimization question for the bouquet of 2k odd cycles of equal length with opposite-sign pairing, so the problem appears to remain open.
